summary: Tara Doyle is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She served at Emory University as a lecturer in religious studies and director of the Tibetan Studies Program (attested 2003), later becoming Professor Emerita (attested 2026).
Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1962–1998) and at the University of Copenhagen (~1970–1998).

Tarthang Tulku (born 1935) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tarthang Monastery and under teachers including Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, later holding posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968) and the Nyingma Institute (~1972).

Tashi Rabgey works in Tibetology. She studied at University College, Toronto, Magdalen College, the University of Cambridge, and Harvard University. She served at the University of Virginia (~2004–2011) and Georgetown University (~2011).

Tashi Samphel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as director at Songtsen Library (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Tashi Tsering (born 1960) works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Educated at Central School for Tibetans and under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, he held posts at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1984–1992) and Amnye Machen Institute (~1992).

Tatiana Oranskaia (born 1950) is an Indologist and linguist. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan, and held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996, 1998–2016).

Tatsugen Sato (1924–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his doctorate from Komazawa University. He served as professor at Komazawa University (~1974–1995) and lectured at Ryukoku University (attested 1974) and Tokai University.

Tatsuo Hayashi (1896–1984) was a philosopher. After studying at Kyoto University (~1917–1921), he held posts at Toyo University (~1925–1932), Tsuda University, Meiji University, Rikkyo University, and Hosei University.

Tatsuo Nishida (1928–2012) was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology who studied at Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Kyoto University and at the National Center for Science Information Systems (1992–1994).

Tatsushi Tamai specializes in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as a visiting researcher at the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology at Soka University (attested 2010–2016).

Tavivat Puntarigvivat (born 1950) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and held posts at Kyoto University, Mahidol University (attested 2005), and the World Buddhist University (attested 2013).
Taw Sein Ko (1864–1930) was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied at the University of Yangon (~1881–1885), the Inner Temple (~1892–1893), and the Inns of Court (~1892–1893).

Teizo Iyanaga (1915–1983) was a scholar of Japanese history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1938) and later held posts at Nagoya University (~1950–1965), the University of Tokyo (~1965–1976), and Sophia University (~1976–1983).

Tej Ram Sharma (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his doctoral thesis at Banaras Hindu University (~1964–1968) and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (~1971).
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Lobsang Gyatso, and also taught Lobsang Gyatso.

Tenga Rinpoche (1932–2012) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Benchen Monastery, founded Benchen Monastery in 1976, and served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery (~1962–1979).

Tensei Kitabatake (1928–2024) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He spent his career at Ryukoku University as a professor and president (1995–1999) before serving as president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye (1938–2003) was a figure in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sogen Omori, whom he succeeded, and founded Chozen-ji.

Tenzin Dhargye (born 1968) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery and Gyume Tantric College, and held posts at the University of Virginia (1999–2000) and Tibetzentrum Österreich (2008).
